claim: Three major non-overlapping classes of interneurons expressing parvalbumin, somatostatin and vasoactive intestinal peptide make up more than 80% of GABAergic cells of mouse cortex.
source: Three major non-overlapping classes of interneurons expressing parvalbumin, somatostatin and vasoactive intestinal peptide (henceforth denoted PV, SST and VIP respectively) make up more than 80% of GABAergic cells of mouse cortex (Rudy et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Rudy et al., 2011.

claim: PV, SST, and VIP neurons show cell-type-specific connectivity among themselves and with excitatory neurons forming a canonical microcircuit in the cortex.
source: These neurons show cell-type-specific connectivity among themselves and with excitatory (E) neurons (Pfeffer et al., 2013; Jiang et al., 2015) forming a canonical microcircuit in the cortex.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Pfeffer et al., 2013 and Jiang et al., 2015.

claim: The canonical microcircuit motif was initially proposed theoretically by Wang et al., 2004.
source: This microcircuit motif, initially proposed theoretically (Wang et al., 2004), has been the subject of numerous recent experimental studies using optogenetic tools applied to behaving mice (Lee et al., 2012; Saleem et al., 2013; Kepecs and Fishell, 2014; Hawrylycz et al., 2016) as well as computational studies (Lee and Mihalas, 2015; Lee and Mihalas, 2017; Lee et al., 2017; Yang et al., 2016; Yang and Wang, 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2004.

claim: Pyramidal neurons and VIP interneurons concomitantly increase their activities in the primary visual cortex V1 during locomotion in comparison with immobility.
source: A notable observation was that pyramidal neurons and VIP interneurons concomitantly increase their activities in the primary visual cortex V1 during locomotion in comparison with immobility (Niell and Stryker, 2010), even in the complete absence of visual input (Keller et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Niell and Stryker, 2010 and Keller et al., 2012.

claim: Pyramidal neurons and VIP interneurons increase their activities during locomotion even in the complete absence of visual input.
source: A notable observation was that pyramidal neurons and VIP interneurons concomitantly increase their activities in the primary visual cortex V1 during locomotion in comparison with immobility (Niell and Stryker, 2010), even in the complete absence of visual input (Keller et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Keller et al., 2012.

claim: Optogenetically activating VIP interneurons mimics the effect of running.
source: Moreover, optogenetically activating (respectively inactivating) VIP interneurons mimics (respectively eliminates) the effect of running (Fu et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Fu et al., 2014.

claim: Optogenetically inactivating VIP interneurons eliminates the effect of running.
source: Moreover, optogenetically activating (respectively inactivating) VIP interneurons mimics (respectively eliminates) the effect of running (Fu et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Fu et al., 2014.

claim: VIP cells primarily target SST cells.
source: Since VIP cells primarily target SST cells, a natural explanation for this phenomenon is disinhibition (Wang et al., 2004; Lee et al., 2013): activation of VIP cells suppresses SST cells, therefore neurons targeted by the SST population are disinhibited, enhancing the overall activity of excitatory neurons.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by the disinhibition mechanism described.

claim: In darkness, the activation of VIP cells results in an average decrease of SST population activity.
source: Namely, in darkness the activation of VIP cells results in an average decrease of SST population activity (Fu et al., 2014), whereas in the presence of visual stimulation the response of SST cells is reversed and its firing rate increases during locomotion compared to immobility (Pakan et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Fu et al., 2014.

claim: In the presence of visual stimulation, the response of SST cells is reversed and its firing rate increases during locomotion compared to immobility.
source: Namely, in darkness the activation of VIP cells results in an average decrease of SST population activity (Fu et al., 2014), whereas in the presence of visual stimulation the response of SST cells is reversed and its firing rate increases during locomotion compared to immobility (Pakan et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Pakan et al., 2016.

claim: The findings about SST response reversal have been further confirmed in a recent preprint by Dipoppa et al., 2017.
source: These findings, which have been further confirmed in a recent preprint (Dipoppa et al., 2017), appear to challenge the disinhibition hypothesis, suggesting that the nature of the interaction between VIP and SST could be stimulus dependent.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Dipoppa et al., 2017.

claim: Counterintuitive phenomena in cortical networks rely on two basic features: the presence of multiple populations of interneurons and nonlinear responses to input.
source: We show that these counterintuitive phenomena rely on two basic features of cortical networks: (i) the presence of multiple populations of interneurons and (ii) nonlinear responses to input.
evidence: The claim is based on the theoretical analysis and modeling presented in the manuscript.

claim: The model uses a four population firing rate model to simulate microcircuit activity.
source: We simulate microcircuit activity using a four population firing rate model.
evidence: The claim describes the computational method used in the study.

claim: The average rate of each population is given by a nonlinear function of its input referred to as the f-I curve.
source: The average rate of each population is given by a nonlinear function of its input that we refer to as the f-I curve (Abbott and Chance, 2005).
evidence: The claim describes the model structure and cites Abbott and Chance, 2005.

claim: When input is low (below threshold), cells are little responsive to changes in external input.
source: The f-I curve is such that when the input is low (below threshold), cells are little responsive to changes in external input.
evidence: The claim describes a property of the f-I curve used in the model.

claim: When input is high (above threshold), small changes in the input can drive substantial changes in the response.
source: Instead for high input (above threshold) small changes in the input can drive substantial changes in the response (Miller and Troyer, 2002) (see Figure 1b).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Miller and Troyer, 2002 and reference to Figure 1b.

claim: The nonlinearity of the f-I curve has been analyzed experimentally and theoretically.
source: This nonlinearity has been analyzed experimentally and theoretically (Murphy and Miller, 2003; Phillips and Hasenstaub, 2016) and as we will show later, it is a key feature of the model.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Murphy and Miller, 2003 and Phillips and Hasenstaub, 2016.

claim: The nonlinearity of the f-I curve is a key feature of the model.
source: This nonlinearity has been analyzed experimentally and theoretically (Murphy and Miller, 2003; Phillips and Hasenstaub, 2016) and as we will show later, it is a key feature of the model.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Populations are connected according to the microcircuit scheme in Figure 1a which contains the connections reported in both Jiang et al., 2015 and Pfeffer et al., 2013.
source: Populations are connected according to the microcircuit scheme in Figure 1a which contains the connections reported in both Jiang et al., 2015 and Pfeffer et al. (2013).
evidence: The claim references Figure 1a and cites Jiang et al., 2015 and Pfeffer et al., 2013.

claim: When baseline activity is low, top-down modulation results in a decrease of the rate of the SST population and an increase of the rates of the other populations (E, PV and VIP).
source: On the one hand, when the baseline activity is low, top-down modulation will result in a decrease of the rate of the SST population and an increase of the rates of the other populations (E, PV and VIP) (see Figure 1c).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 1c.

claim: When baseline activity is high, the rate of all populations increases with top-down modulation.
source: On the other hand, when baseline activity is high, the rate of all populations increases with top-down modulation (see Figure 1d).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 1d.

claim: Population responses to top-down modulation depend in a complex way on the initial state of the network.
source: These simulations reveal that population responses to top-down modulation depend in a complex way on the initial state of the network.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the simulation results.

claim: When baseline activity is low, the E population is below threshold and changes in net input have a small effect on the output.
source: When baseline activity is low the E population is below threshold and this change in net input has a small effect in the output.
evidence: The claim is based on the model's f-I curve properties and simulation results.

claim: When baseline activity is high, the E population is above threshold and a small change in input from SST cells has a big effect on the rate of the E population.
source: However, when the baseline activity is high, the E population is above threshold and a small change in input from SST cells has a big effect on the rate of the E population.
evidence: The claim is based on the model's f-I curve properties and simulation results.

claim: If the recurrent excitation in the microcircuit is strong enough, it can reverse the initial response of the SST population making it increase its activity to a higher rate than the baseline.
source: If the recurrent excitation in the microcircuit is strong enough, it can reverse the initial response of the SST population making it increase its activity to a higher rate than the baseline.
evidence: The claim is based on the model's dynamics and simulation results.

claim: Due to the nonlinearities in the f-I curve, the response depends on the baseline rate of each of the populations and can reverse its sign.
source: Furthermore, due to the nonlinearities in the f-I curve, the response depends on the baseline rate of each of the populations and, as shown before, it can reverse its sign.
evidence: The claim is based on the mathematical analysis and simulation results.

claim: Modifying the state of one population has an impact on the interactions between other populations.
source: It is remarkable that this change in the interaction between VIP and SST populations depends on the activation level of E: modifying the state of one population has a impact in the interactions between other populations.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the mathematical analysis.

claim: If the recurrent excitation is strong enough and the E population is strongly excited (above threshold), a small decrease in the inhibition from SST to the E population can boost its activity and strongly drive the whole microcircuit.
source: The heuristic explanation is that if the recurrent excitation is strong enough and the E population is already strongly excited (above threshold), a small decrease in the inhibition from SST to the E population can boost its activity and therefore strongly drive the whole microcircuit.
evidence: The claim provides a mechanistic explanation based on the model.

claim: If the E population is in a low activation state, the change in inhibition will have a weak effect that will not be able to reverse the response of SST.
source: If instead, the E population is in a low activation state the change in inhibition will have a weak effect that will not be able to reverse the response of SST.
evidence: The claim provides a mechanistic explanation based on the model.

claim: For high baseline activity, the response of the SST population to input to VIP cells becomes positive leading to the response reversal regime.
source: On the other hand, for high baseline activity (panels 2b and 2d), the response of the SST population to input to VIP cells becomes positive leading to the response reversal regime.
evidence: The claim is supported by the analysis and Figure 2b and d.

claim: Experimental recordings showed a great diversity across neural responses even when recording from the same class of cells.
source: Experimental recordings showed a great diversity across neural responses even when recording from the same class of cells (Pyramidal, SST, PV or VIP) (Pakan et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Pakan et al., 2016.

claim: Random connectivity alone is sufficient to explain the diversity in neural responses.
source: Although this diversity can have many origins, such as intrinsic heterogeneity in the cells within the same class, we proposed that random connectivity alone is sufficient to explain it.
evidence: The claim is a hypothesis proposed by the authors and tested in their model.

claim: In the random network model, each population is composed of multiple identical randomly connected rate units.
source: To do so we develop an extension of our model where each population is composed of multiple identical randomly connected rate units and where the probability that one connection exists from one unit to another depends on the populations of the presynaptic and postsynaptic units according to data extracted from Jiang et al. (2015); Pfeffer et al. (2013) (see Materials and methods for details).
evidence: The claim describes the structure of the random network model.

claim: The probability that one connection exists from one unit to another depends on the populations of the presynaptic and postsynaptic units according to data extracted from Jiang et al. (2015); Pfeffer et al. (2013).
source: To do so we develop an extension of our model where each population is composed of multiple identical randomly connected rate units and where the probability that one connection exists from one unit to another depends on the populations of the presynaptic and postsynaptic units according to data extracted from Jiang et al. (2015); Pfeffer et al. (2013) (see Materials and methods for details).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Jiang et al., 2015 and Pfeffer et al., 2013.

claim: The behavior of individual neurons can be quite variable while the population average still corresponds to the behavior of the population-based model.
source: These simulations reveal that the behavior of individual neurons can be quite variable while the population average still corresponds to the behavior of the population-based model.
evidence: The claim is based on simulation results from the random network model.

claim: Since all units of each population are identical, variability in the response has to be due to the heterogeneity in the connectivity.
source: Since all units of each population are identical, variability in the response has to be due to the heterogeneity in the connectivity.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the model structure.

claim: Variability in connectivity can result in cells within the same population having responses with opposite sign, as has been observed in mouse V1.
source: This variability can result in cells within the same population having responses with opposite sign, as has been observed to be the case in mouse V1 (Reimer et al., 2014; Pakan et al., 2016) and A1 (Kuchibhotla et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Reimer et al., 2014, Pakan et al., 2016, and Kuchibhotla et al., 2017.

claim: Variability in inhibitory cells has been proposed to modulate the response gain of neural circuits.
source: In addition, variability might also have further implications for gating of signals, since variability in inhibitory cells has been proposed to modulate the response gain of neural circuits (Mejias and Longtin, 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Mejias and Longtin, 2014.

claim: In the experiments, mice with their head fixed face a screen where different visual stimuli are presented and can run freely on a treadmill.
source: In the experiments mice with their head fixed face a screen where different visual stimuli are presented and can run freely on a treadmill (Fu et al., 2014; Pakan et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim describes the experimental setup and is supported by citations to Fu et al., 2014 and Pakan et al., 2016.

claim: Different visual stimuli result in different baseline activities in V1.
source: Different visual stimuli result in different baseline activities in V1 and top-down modulation is triggered when the mice start running.
evidence: The claim is based on the experimental observations and model interpretation.

claim: Top-down modulation is triggered when the mice start running.
source: Different visual stimuli result in different baseline activities in V1 and top-down modulation is triggered when the mice start running.
evidence: The claim is based on the experimental observations.

claim: In the model of size-varying gratings, visual input has two sources: thalamic input that targets excitatory cells and cortical input that targets SST cells.
source: To model visual input we use external currents. In the case of size-varying gratings, this input has two sources: thalamic input that targets excitatory cells and cortical input that targets SST cells.
evidence: The claim describes the model structure.

claim: In order to reproduce the surround suppression effect, excitatory cells have a small receptive field and receive center input, and SST cells have a large receptive field and receive surround input.
source: In order to reproduce the surround suppression effect (Ozeki et al., 2009; Adesnik et al., 2012), excitatory cells have a small receptive field and therefore receive center input and SST cells have a large receptive field and receive surround input (see Materials and methods for details).
evidence: The claim describes the model structure and cites Ozeki et al., 2009 and Adesnik et al., 2012.

claim: Before the visual stimulation, the SST has higher activity for immobility than for locomotion.
source: Figure 4b shows the response reversal phenomenon when a weak visual stimulus is presented. Before the visual stimulation, the SST has higher activity for immobility than for locomotion, by contrast, when the visual stimulus is presented, the activity of the SST population is higher for locomotion.
evidence: The claim is supported by Figure 4b.

claim: When the visual stimulus is presented, the activity of the SST population is higher for locomotion.
source: Figure 4b shows the response reversal phenomenon when a weak visual stimulus is presented. Before the visual stimulation, the SST has higher activity for immobility than for locomotion, by contrast, when the visual stimulus is presented, the activity of the SST population is higher for locomotion.
evidence: The claim is supported by Figure 4b.

claim: The simulations of the V1 circuit model reproduce the phenomena described in the literature.
source: Our simulations of this V1 circuit model reproduce the phenomena described in the literature: in the presence of visual stimulation, the activities of all populations, including SST, increase during locomotion (Pakan et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of simulation results with experimental data.

claim: In the presence of visual stimulation, the activities of all populations, including SST, increase during locomotion.
source: Our simulations of this V1 circuit model reproduce the phenomena described in the literature: in the presence of visual stimulation, the activities of all populations, including SST, increase during locomotion (Pakan et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Pakan et al., 2016 and simulation results.

claim: In darkness, the activities of excitatory, PV and VIP populations increase during locomotion while the activity of SST decreases as reported in Fu et al. (2014) and in the preprint (Dipoppa et al., 2017).
source: In darkness, the activities of excitatory, PV and VIP populations increase during locomotion while the activity of SST decreases as reported in Fu et al. (2014) and in the preprint (Dipoppa et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Fu et al., 2014 and Dipoppa et al., 2017, and simulation results.

claim: In Pakan et al. (2016), the response of SST to locomotion in darkness is weakly positive but this result is not statistically significant.
source: In Pakan et al. (2016), the response of SST to locomotion in darkness is weakly positive but this result is not statistically significant while the other two are.
evidence: The claim is based on the experimental results reported in Pakan et al., 2016.

claim: The results do not rely on a fine tuning of the connectivity parameters or on certain details of the microcircuit structure.
source: To show that our results do not rely on a fine tuning of the connectivity parameters or even on certain details of the microcircuit structure, we have run the model with several connectivity matrices and perturbations of them (Figure 4—figure supplement 2) and we find that different connectivity parameters can reproduce the same circuit behavior as has been shown before in other systems (Marder et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulations with different connectivity matrices shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2 and citation to Marder et al., 2015.

claim: Different connectivity parameters can reproduce the same circuit behavior as has been shown before in other systems.
source: To show that our results do not rely on a fine tuning of the connectivity parameters or even on certain details of the microcircuit structure, we have run the model with several connectivity matrices and perturbations of them (Figure 4—figure supplement 2) and we find that different connectivity parameters can reproduce the same circuit behavior as has been shown before in other systems (Marder et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Marder et al., 2015 and simulation results.

claim: The phenomenon and the analysis are robust and not a peculiarity of one specific circuit.
source: In all these cases, the results were consistent with our original findings showing that the phenomenon and the analysis are robust and not a peculiarity of one specific circuit.
evidence: The claim is based on simulations with different circuit structures.

claim: Two features of the system lead to the counterintuitive behavior: the presence of multiple interneuron populations and the nonlinearity of f-I curves.
source: We have developed a theoretical model of cortical circuit with multiple interneuron types that accounts for newly identified complex interactions between cell types. The model has been used to reproduce and explain two counterintuitive phenomena observed in mouse cortex. First, in certain cases the activation of VIP cells results in an overall positive response of the SST population (Pakan et al., 2016). Second, the sign of the SST population response to excitation of VIP cells depends on the baseline activity of the circuit (Fu et al., 2014). Two features of the system lead to this behavior: the presence of multiple interneuron populations and the nonlinearity of f-I curves.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion from the theoretical analysis and modeling.

claim: In the response reversal regime, the overall SST population response to top-down modulation should initially decrease and later increase until reaching a higher rate than the baseline.
source: One experimentally testable prediction of our analysis is that, as Figure 1d and our calculations of the transient behavior show, in the response reversal regime, the overall SST population response to top-down modulation should initially decrease and later increase until reaching a higher rate than the baseline.
evidence: The claim is a prediction based on the model and Figure 1d.

claim: This statement can be easily tested by repeating the experiments while suppressing the activation of the E population.
source: This statement can be easily tested by repeating the experiments while suppressing the activation of the E population.
evidence: The claim is a prediction for experimental testing.

claim: In the regime where SST activity has a positive response to excitatory input targeting VIP, SST has to have a negative response to external input targeting SST.
source: This predicts that in the regime where SST activity has a positive response to excitatory input targeting VIP, SST has to have a negative response to external input targeting SST.
evidence: The claim is a prediction based on the sign correlation between M_SV and M_SS.

claim: VIP interneurons play an important role in cortical activity modulation.
source: In addition, our results are in line with experimental studies that show that VIP interneurons play an important role in cortical activity modulation (Mesik et al., 2015; Ibrahim et al., 2016; Jackson et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Mesik et al., 2015, Ibrahim et al., 2016, and Jackson et al., 2016.

claim: For the given microcircuit structure, all terms of the response matrix can be positive or negative.
source: The analysis of the response matrix shows that for the given microcircuit structure all terms of the matrix can be positive or negative.
evidence: The claim is based on the mathematical analysis of the response matrix.

claim: Having more than one inhibitory population results in a much more versatile network.
source: In this sense, having more than one inhibitory population results in a much more versatile network.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the comparison between multi-interneuron and E-I networks.

claim: In networks with more than one inhibitory population, the relationship between response reversal and ISN is not necessarily bidirectional.
source: When analysing networks with more than one inhibitory population the relationship is not necessarily bidirectional any more.
evidence: The claim is based on the mathematical analysis of multi-interneuron networks.

claim: This study provides a parsimonious yet powerful explanation to striking observations of interneuronal circuits in V1 without requiring the assumption of top-down excitatory inputs explicitly targeting SST or PV neurons.
source: Finally, this study provides a parsimonious yet powerful explanation to striking observations of interneuronal circuits in V1 (Fu et al., 2014; Pakan et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2017) without requiring the assumption of top-down excitatory inputs explicitly targeting SST or PV neurons.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion from the modeling work and cites Fu et al., 2014, Pakan et al., 2016, and Lee et al., 2017.

claim: The computational neural network model and the response matrix analysis go beyond circuit dynamics in mice V1 and can be easily applied to other species and cortical areas.
source: Both our computational neural network model and the approach presented here (the response matrix analysis) go beyond circuit dynamics in mice V1 and can be easily applied to other species and cortical areas.
evidence: The claim is a statement about the generalizability of the approach.

claim: The approach naturally explains the response reversal observed in cat visual cortex.
source: By extending previous works (Tsodyks et al., 1997; Ozeki et al., 2009), it naturally explains the response reversal observed in cat visual cortex (Ozeki et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Tsodyks et al., 1997 and Ozeki et al., 2009.

claim: The approach could be applied to explain similar phenomena observed in mouse primary auditory cortex.
source: It could also be applied to explain similar phenomena observed in mouse primary auditory cortex (Seybold et al., 2015; Kuchibhotla et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is a speculation supported by citations to Seybold et al., 2015 and Kuchibhotla et al., 2017.

claim: In Kuchibhotla et al. (2017), the authors find that locomotion reduces the activity of excitatory cells.
source: In particular, in Kuchibhotla et al. (2017), the authors find that locomotion reduces the activity of excitatory cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Kuchibhotla et al., 2017.

claim: In mouse somatosensory cortex, activating VIP neurons results in an intuitive decrease in SST activity, instead of a response reversal.
source: In mouse somatosensory cortex, activating VIP neurons results in an intuitive decrease in SST activity, instead of a response reversal (Lee et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2013.

claim: The qualitative difference between V1 and somatosensory cortex may be explained by the quantitative difference between their circuit architectures.
source: As our results suggest, this qualitative difference between V1 and somatosensory cortex may be explained by the quantitative difference between their circuit architectures: in a recent study the authors showed that cell densities of different types of interneurons differ substantially across cortical areas resulting in counterintuitive impacts on circuit responses (Kim et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is a speculation supported by a citation to Kim et al., 2017.

claim: Cell densities of different types of interneurons differ substantially across cortical areas resulting in counterintuitive impacts on circuit responses.
source: As our results suggest, this qualitative difference between V1 and somatosensory cortex may be explained by the quantitative difference between their circuit architectures: in a recent study the authors showed that cell densities of different types of interneurons differ substantially across cortical areas resulting in counterintuitive impacts on circuit responses (Kim et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Kim et al., 2017.

claim: Neural responses in many cortical areas, including primary auditory cortex, are largely transient and dynamical.
source: In this work, we mainly focused on steady-state responses. However, neural responses in many cortical areas, including primary auditory cortex, are largely transient and dynamical (Wehr and Zador, 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Wehr and Zador, 2003.

claim: Synaptic connections to and from interneurons are often subject to short-term plasticity.
source: In addition, synaptic connections to and from interneurons are often subject to short-term plasticity (Reyes et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Reyes et al., 1998.

claim: Understanding transient dynamics in nonlinear, multi-type interneuronal circuits would be an important topic for future research.
source: Understanding transient dynamics in nonlinear, multi-type interneuronal circuits would be an important topic for future research.
evidence: The claim is a statement about future research directions.

claim: The presence of a single inhibitory neuron type can cause paradoxical effects.
source: We have shown that similar to the now well-known paradoxical effect that the presence of a single inhibitory neuron type can cause (Tsodyks et al., 1997; Ozeki et al., 2009), the presence of multiple types of interneurons has an even stronger impact on the activity of neural circuits.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Tsodyks et al., 1997 and Ozeki et al., 2009.

claim: The presence of multiple types of interneurons has an even stronger impact on the activity of neural circuits than a single inhibitory neuron type.
source: We have shown that similar to the now well-known paradoxical effect that the presence of a single inhibitory neuron type can cause (Tsodyks et al., 1997; Ozeki et al., 2009), the presence of multiple types of interneurons has an even stronger impact on the activity of neural circuits.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion from the analysis comparing single and multiple interneuron types.

claim: In a circuit with multiple populations, the most interesting circuit behavior is found when spontaneous baseline activity is close to threshold.
source: Our analysis suggests that in a circuit with multiple populations, the most interesting circuit behavior is found when spontaneous baseline activity is close to threshold since in that regime responses will change the most with small changes in population rates.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the analysis of the model.

claim: The two features (multiple populations and nonlinearity) significantly broaden the richness of the dynamics of cortical circuits and enhance their usefulness for cognitive and behavioral computations.
source: These two features significantly broaden the richness of the dynamics of cortical circuits and enhance their usefulness for cognitive and behavioral computations.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion from the analysis.

claim: Computational models and mathematical analysis are critical to fully understand the dynamics of neural circuits underlying behavior, especially when several types of interneurons are involved.
source: We conclude that computational models and mathematical analysis are critical to fully understand the dynamics of neural circuits underlying behavior (Gjorgjieva et al., 2016), especially when several types of interneurons are involved as intuition alone may be misleading and provide erroneous predictions on such circuits.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion supported by a citation to Gjorgjieva et al., 2016.

claim: Intuition alone may be misleading and provide erroneous predictions on circuits with several types of interneurons.
source: We conclude that computational models and mathematical analysis are critical to fully understand the dynamics of neural circuits underlying behavior (Gjorgjieva et al., 2016), especially when several types of interneurons are involved as intuition alone may be misleading and provide erroneous predictions on such circuits.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion from the analysis.
